issues.description: FAQ example complects request validation with stream-reading semantics
issues.detail: The PostTest handler tangles three concerns: deciding whether a body exists, reading the stream, and choosing a status code. The nested if/else with req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0) hides what the example is actually demonstrating (header overrides). A simpler form would separate 'read body' from 'decide status' as two pure steps.

issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream is the real fix, but it is undocumented
issues.detail: The one-line change in things_advanced.py is the load-bearing semantic shift: bounded_stream respects Content-Length so an empty body with a lying header no longer hangs or misreads. That is the actual value/time fact this PR encodes. It deserves a comment or news fragment, not just a silent diff.

issues.description: Test asserts status code without asserting the underlying fact
issues.detail: resp4 checks status_code == 400 but never confirms which guard fired. An empty body with Content-Length: 1 could 400 for several reasons (bounded_stream returns empty, JSON parse fails, body check fails). The test passes today but does not pin down the behavior it claims to protect. Assert the error title or body too.

issues.description: README diff conflates reformatting with behavior changes
issues.detail: The README hunk mixes pure whitespace/quote reformatting with two real semantic edits: StorageError.handle argument order changed and resp.status now uses falcon.code_to_http_status. These are different concerns and should not ride in a test PR; they make the diff hard to reason about and the time-of-change for each fact unclear.

issues.description: Magic path '/1337/things' is incidental and undocumented
issues.detail: The integer 1337 is a value with no explanation, repeated across tests. It is incidental complexity in the test text. A named constant (USER_ID = '1337') would make the value explicit and separate 'which user' from 'what we are testing'.

issues.description: The question that should have been asked first: why does Content-Length lie?
issues.detail: The PR adds tests for a client sending Content-Length: 1 with an empty body. Before adding the guard, the design question is whether bounded_stream alone is the correct contract and whether the JSONTranslator should trust headers at all. The fix is correct, but the framing treats a symptom (test the case) rather than naming the invariant (body is whatever bounded_stream yields, header is advisory).

review.summary: The substantive change is one line: req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read(). That is the real fact about the world this PR encodes — Content-Length is advisory, the bounded stream is authoritative — but it ships silently alongside a large README reformatting hunk and a FAQ example that complects validation with stream-reading. The new tests are useful but assert status codes without pinning down which guard fired, so they will pass for the wrong reasons under future refactoring. Simple move: separate the bounded_stream semantic change (with a news fragment and a comment) from the README cosmetic churn, and tighten the assertions to name the fact being protected.
